claims.text: Conventional elemental Cr coatings provide oxidation protection to zirconium-alloy cladding.
Cr-coated zirconium-alloy cladding suffers interdiffusion-induced coating failure at elevated temperatures.
A thin ZrN interlayer can be deposited between zirconium-alloy cladding and an elemental Cr coating.
The deposited ZrN interlayer will remain continuous at the Cr–Zr interface.
ZrN is stable at the high temperatures relevant to the proposed accident exposure.
ZrN has sufficiently low Cr and Zr diffusivity to act as a diffusion barrier at the Cr–Zr interface.
The ZrN interlayer will impede Cr–Zr interdiffusion at elevated temperatures.
Reduced Cr–Zr interdiffusion will help maintain adhesion of the Cr coating.
Reduced Cr–Zr interdiffusion will preserve the protective oxide properties of the overlying Cr layer.
Relative to directly Cr-coated cladding, the ZrN-containing system will exhibit less Cr–Zr interdiffusion.
Relative to directly Cr-coated cladding, the ZrN-containing system will exhibit slower interfacial oxide-layer growth.
Relative to directly Cr-coated cladding, the ZrN-containing system will exhibit improved mechanical integrity.
The ZrN interlayer will extend Cr-coating lifetime.
The ZrN-containing coating will provide consistent oxidation protection during both normal subcritical-water service and accident-relevant high-temperature steam exposure.
The proposed normal-operation boundary is subcritical water below approximately 400°C over long-duration exposure.
The proposed accident boundary is transient steam exposure at approximately 1100–1200°C.
Performance significantly outside the stated temperature ranges is uncertain.
Long-term stability of the ZrN interlayer under prolonged neutron irradiation is uncertain.
